raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From 29 Washington Place, carry on to Stonewall Inn, about a 16-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The blocks you're leaving keep their own quiet history.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"At 82 Washington Place, Willa Cather lived with Edith Lewis from about 1908 to 1913 — the writer who'd give us My Ántonia and Death Comes for the Archbishop, who signed her college letters 'William,' and who shared her life with Lewis for nearly forty years until her death in 1947, then destroyed most of her correspondence before she went.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"A few streets on, at 86 University Place, the Bagatelle was one of the only lesbian bars in 1950s New York, and Audre Lorde wrote it into Zami: A New Spelling of My Name, remembering that 'the Bag was always The Club.'","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Look at No. 53 — the bar that stood here, the Stonewall Inn, was nothing fancy, crowded on weekends and, like most bars serving a gay crowd, owned by the Mob, which paid off the police.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Raids and shakedowns were routine, and a light over the door flashed when the cops were coming.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"In the early morning hours of June 28, 1969, the patrons fought back.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"When police singled out several drag queens for arrest and shoved the rest into the street, one butch lesbian struck the officer who'd hit her, and the crowd let loose a hail of coins and invective.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The cops were driven back inside, the crowd attacked the building and tried to set it on fire, and the police drew their guns.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Riot police averted a shooting, but the crowd would not back down.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Those nights of unrest launched a new phase of activism — gay liberation.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"This stretch of Christopher Street proclaims itself the birthplace of the modern lesbian and gay rights movement, where that police raid sparked the clash near Christopher Park that began the fight for equal rights.","source_id":"96628e6b-52d2-439d-944e-056fcb6d9f6e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["9e364a3b-9eca-42ed-b808-c97f769a2658","7d61972e-4dfd-4ddc-aefe-4d13daee1757"]},{"text":"Since then the park and its surroundings have become a symbol of gay liberation, and the street around you is lined with LGBTQ bars and shops.","source_id":"7d61972e-4dfd-4ddc-aefe-4d13daee1757","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"On the riots' first anniversary, New York held its first Gay Pride march, up Sixth Avenue from Christopher Street to Central Park — and every June since, the world has remembered with parades.","source_id":"41abaca7-dc30-41d9-a54d-2f45a3e375b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"As one activist quipped, he was probably one of six people who lived in the Village at the time who didn't claim to have been at the Stonewall riots.","source_id":"41abaca7-dc30-41d9-a54d-2f45a3e375b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The uprising spurred two organizations: the Gay Liberation Front, launched immediately after, and the Gay Activists Alliance, which split off in December 1969 after infighting over how far the work should reach.","source_id":"41abaca7-dc30-41d9-a54d-2f45a3e375b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The GLF saw itself as part of the New Left and pushed coalition politics, while the GAA's constitution barred any alliance with a group not directly tied to the homosexual cause.","source_id":"41abaca7-dc30-41d9-a54d-2f45a3e375b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Together they answered homophobia with 'zap' actions and forced a new visibility.","source_id":"41abaca7-dc30-41d9-a54d-2f45a3e375b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The first GLF meetings met at Alternate U, at 534 Sixth Avenue, and from 1971 to 1974 the GAA ran out of a renovated firehouse at 99 Wooster Street — a center of gay life until it was firebombed in October 1974, amid a rash of arson attacks on gay bars, homes, and offices.","source_id":"41abaca7-dc30-41d9-a54d-2f45a3e375b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"In 1999 the blocks around the former inn became a National Historic Landmark — the Stonewall National Historic District, the first time the federal government recognized lesbian and gay history.","source_id":"d3e6b9bd-6c3b-46e0-8a03-e6adcd9a18bd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The bar standing here now, called Stonewall, isn't the original, though it keeps the room alive with gay cabaret, karaoke, and comedy.","source_id":"d3e6b9bd-6c3b-46e0-8a03-e6adcd9a18bd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["9e364a3b-9eca-42ed-b808-c97f769a2658"]},{"text":"In 2016, President Barack Obama went further, naming the Stonewall Inn, Christopher Park, and the surrounding streets a national monument — the first ever to honor the LGBTIQ+ civil rights movement.","source_id":"53989fd3-a54a-4b71-9f1e-dcf6a2a112e9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["f2277565-c180-4885-91da-6fad118be95b"]},{"text":"Rangers stationed in the park, and the memorials around it, now tell more of the story.","source_id":"53989fd3-a54a-4b71-9f1e-dcf6a2a112e9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"And if you want the Village's other heartbeat, walk to Smalls at 183 West 10th Street — a hole-in-the-wall basement that still puts up-and-coming talent on its tiny stage.","source_id":"030cd583-aa66-4b78-823e-99d3fb952dda","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2}]}
